items.prompt: White to move. The king stands on h1. Tap every square it could step to.

claims.statement: The king on h1 can go to g1 only.

hints: Count the squares next to the king: how many are empty?
The pawns on g2 and h2 are the king's own pieces.
Only the square beside the king on the first rank is free.
items.explain: A king in the corner behind two pawns has a single free square. A rook check along the first rank covers it at once.

items.prompt: White to move. Black threatens to give mate on the first rank. Play a move that holds.

claims.statement: Seven moves hold: pawn moves that give the king a square, or a king step.
Taking the pawn on a7 loses to a forced mate.
Offering a trade on the d-file loses a rook.

hints: Which Black piece is aimed at your first rank?
Your rook is far from the first rank. Can you give the king a square?
A pawn move in front of the king, or a king step, answers the threat.
items.explain: Black threatens Rd1 mate. A pawn move gives the king air, and a king step to f1 also works here. Grabbing the pawn on a7 leaves the rank unguarded.

feedback_by_move.a3a7: The rook takes a pawn and Black plays Rd1, which is mate: nothing guards the first rank.
feedback_by_move.a3d3: Black simply takes the rook: Rxd3 wins a whole rook.
feedback_by_move.b2b3: A quiet move does not answer the threat: Rd1 is mate.

items.prompt: White to move. Black threatens a mate on the first rank. Play a move that holds; several do.

claims.statement: These eight moves all hold.
A quiet pawn move loses to mate.
Taking the pawn on a7 loses to mate.

hints: Which black piece can reach your first rank next move?
You can give the king a square or put a piece on the rank.
Pawn moves that give the king a square, a king step and the rook retreat all work.
items.explain: The holding moves answer the threat by air for the king or a guard on the rank. A quiet move elsewhere does not.

feedback_by_move.b2b3: A move on the queenside does not touch the threat: Rd1 is mate.
feedback_by_move.a3a7: The rook takes a pawn but leaves the first rank to Black: Rd1 is mate.

items.prompt: White to move. Does White need to make luft right now?

claims.statement: If White passes, Black has Rd1 mate.
No white piece covers d1.

hints: Which black piece can reach your first rank?
Is anything of yours covering the square the rook would use?
Rd1 would be mate if you pass.
items.explain: The rook can reach d1 and nothing guards it, so White has to act now.

items.prompt: White to move. Does White need to make luft right now?

claims.statement: If White passes, Rd1 is not mate.
The bishop covers d1.

hints: Which black piece can reach your first rank?
Is anything of yours covering the square the rook would use?
The bishop covers d1.
items.explain: The bishop covers d1, so Rd1 would just lose a rook. There is no need to spend a move.

items.prompt: White to move. Does Rxd8+ lead to checkmate?

claims.statement: White mates in two moves.
Black has one defender of d8: the rook on a8.

hints: How many black pieces guard d8?
How many white rooks can take on d8, one after another?
Two attackers against one defender.
items.explain: Black has one defender and White has two rooks. After the first rook is taken, the second takes and nothing is left.

items.prompt: White to move. Does Rxd8+ lead to checkmate?

claims.statement: Rxd8 is not mate.
Black has two defenders of d8: the rook on a8 and the bishop.

hints: How many black pieces guard d8?
How many white rooks can take on d8, one after another?
Two attackers against two defenders: who captures last?
items.explain: Black has a second defender, the bishop. White runs out of rooks first, so the exchange only trades pieces.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The rook check wins material.
The rook check is the best move.

hints: Which of your pieces can reach the first rank?
Which white pieces can answer a check on e1?
Check, and see what is forced.
items.explain: The rook check can only be answered by the queen, which then falls for the rook. The back-rank threat wins material without mate.

items.prompt: White to move. What does Black threaten? Move a black piece to show it.

claims.statement: If White passes, Re1 is checkmate.
No white piece covers e1.

hints: Which black pieces can reach a square near your king?
Count your king's escape squares.
The rook on the open file reaches e1.
items.explain: The rook has the open file and nothing guards e1, so Black threatens Re1 mate. This is the same pattern seen from the defender's side.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a mate in one?

claims.statement: The rook check is answered by a capture and the rook is lost.
A white piece covers e1.

hints: Which square would the rook check on?
Can White take a piece that lands there?
The knight covers e1.
items.explain: The rook can check on e1, but the knight takes it. A back-rank check is not mate if the checking piece can be taken.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a mate in one?

claims.statement: Re8 is not mate.
Two black pieces cover f8: the bishop and the king.

hints: Which square would the rook check on?
Can Black step in between?
The bishop covers f8.
items.explain: The rook can check on e8, but the bishop interposes on f8. The check is parried, so it is not mate.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a mate in one?

claims.statement: Re8 is not mate.
The king can step to g7: no white piece attacks it.

hints: Which square would the rook check on?
Count the king's escape squares.
The pawn moved from g7 to g6.
items.explain: The rook can check on e8, but the king steps to g7. A flight square is enough to rule the mate out.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a mate in one?

claims.statement: The rook cannot reach e1: the pawn on e4 blocks the file.

hints: Which square would the rook check on?
Can the rook get there?
Look at the e-file.
items.explain: A back-rank mate needs a checking piece that can actually reach the rank. Here the pawn on e4 blocks the file, so there is no check at all.
